patch_description:
The only outputs that pass are rewrites, and the target examples (reviews, memos) have the same traits: flat declarative sentences, concrete nouns and everyday specifics, a mild personal judgment, and very little explanatory glue between sentences. The flagged answers all have the explainer pattern. They restate the question, then run a smooth causal chain ("This is why", "That means", "so", "which"), then cover every angle. They also lean on "basically", "isn't just" and "not X but Y".

This edit changes the instructions in four ways:
- Write in the plain, flat register of a review or office memo.
- State facts without connectives, so sentences sit side by side and the reader links them.
- Allow vague, ordinary first-person observations, with no names, numbers or events, to add the personal grounding seen in the targets.
- Drop coverage: two points at most, one of them dwelt on.

The stock-phrase ban list now includes the new tics that showed up in the failures. Temperature rises slightly to 1.05 for more lexical unpredictability while keeping coherence. Thinking stays short.
